The '''15th Academy Awards''' was held in the [[Cocoanut Grove (Ambassador Hotel)|Cocoanut Grove]] at [[Ambassador Hotel (Los Angeles)|The Ambassador Hotel]] in [[Los Angeles]] on March 4, 1943, honoring the [[1942 in film|films of 1942]].<ref name="Oscars1943">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1943/03/05/archives/film-oscar-prize-for-mrs-miniver-the-mgm-picture-featuring-greer.html |title=FILM 'OSCAR' PRIZE FOR 'MRS. MINIVER'; The MGM Picture, Featuring Greer Garson and Walter Pidgeon, Best for 1942 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=March 5, 1943 |access-date=August 15, 2023}}</ref> The ceremony is most famous for the speech by [[Greer Garson]]. Accepting the award for [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]], Garson spoke for approximately 5 minutes and 30 seconds, which was the [[Oscar speech|longest acceptance speech in Oscars history]] until [[Adrien Brody]] won for [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]] in [[97th Academy Awards|2025]].<ref name="Oscars '42 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/836/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=836 |isbn=0-385-04060-1}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/life/features/and-the-oscar-for-the-longest-speech-goes-to-greer-garson/35516692.html |title=And the Oscar for the longest speech goes to ... Greer Garson |work=[[Belfast Telegraph]] |date=March 11, 2017 |access-date=March 3, 2020}}</ref> A portion of the ceremony was broadcast by [[CBS Radio]].<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EwtRbXNca0oC&dq=%22The+Academy+Awards+Show%22&pg=PA4 |title=On the Air: The Encyclopedia of Old-Time Radio |last=Dunning |first=John |author-link=John Dunning (detective fiction author) |date=1998 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |location=[[New York City|New York, NY]] |isbn=978-0-19-507678-3 |pages=4–5 |edition=Revised |access-date=September 9, 2019}}</ref>

''[[Mrs. Miniver]]'' was the second film (after ''[[My Man Godfrey]]'' in [[8th Academy Awards|1936]]) to receive [[List of films with all four Academy Award acting nominations|nominations in all four acting categories]], as well as the first film to receive five acting nominations; it won six of its twelve nominations, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]] and [[William Wyler]]'s first of three [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] awards.<ref name="Oscars1943"/><ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://ew.com/oscars/2018/03/04/oscar-flashback-mrs-miniver-won-big-75-years-ago-and-its-message-of-resistance-endures/ |title=Oscar Flashback: 'Mrs. Miniver' won big 75 years ago — and its message of resistance endures |last=Breznican |first=Anthony |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=March 3, 2018 |access-date=August 15, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goldderby.com/article/2022/oscars-1943/ |title=Oscars flashback to 1943: Patriotic fare fares well |last=King |first=Susan |publisher=GoldDerby |date=September 18, 2022 |access-date=August 15, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://collider.com/directors-with-most-oscars/#william-wyler-mdash-three-awards |title=10 Directors Who Have Won More Than One Directing Oscar |last=Ciriaco |first=Andrea |work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |date=February 1, 2023 |access-date=August 15, 2023}}</ref>

[[Irving Berlin]] presented the [[Academy Award for Best Original Song]], which he ended up winning himself for "[[White Christmas (song)|White Christmas]]".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/movies/moviesnow/la-et-mn-oscars-2016-the-winner-is-me-20160228-story.html |title=For Oscars presenter Irving Berlin, the original-song winner was like an old friend |last=King |first=Susan |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=February 28, 2016 |access-date=August 15, 2023}}</ref> There was also a four-way tie for [[Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature Film|Best Documentary Feature]], a unique occurrence.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goldderby.com/article/2023/1943-oscars-history/ |title=Oscars flashback to the first documentary race: 25 nominees and 4 winners in 1943 |last=King |first=Susan |publisher=GoldDerby |date=January 25, 2023 |access-date=August 15, 2023}}</ref>

===Special awards===
* To [[Charles Boyer]] for his progressive cultural achievement in establishing the French Research Foundation in Los Angeles as a source of reference for the [[Cinema of the United States|Hollywood Motion Picture Industry]].
* To [[Noël Coward]] for his outstanding production achievement in ''[[In Which We Serve]]''.
* To [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer]] for its achievement in representing the American Way of Life in the production of the ''[[Andy Hardy]]'' series of films.

== Ceremony information ==
William Wyler was the first person born in 20th century to win the best director. This ceremony was the last to include a banquet as part of the festivities due to increased attendance and the continuance of [[World War II]]. Ceremonies would be held in theaters starting with the [[16th Academy Awards]] in 1944.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.oscars.org/sites/oscars/files/88aa_presentation_history.pdf |title=History of the Oscars Presentation |publisher=Oscars.org |access-date=May 3, 2023}}</ref> Because of wartime commitments, the usually gold-plated Oscar was made of plaster for this ceremony.<ref name="Oscars '42 Notes"/>
